Manual

The Company Employment Policy Manual
This manual is designed to acquaint and provide employees with information about working conditions,
Employee benefits, and the policies affecting employment.
Employees must read, understand, and comply with all provisions of the Employment Policy Manual
No Employee manual can anticipate every circumstance or question about policy. As The Company
continues to grow, the need may arise, and The Company reserves the right to revise, supplement, or
rescind any policies or portion of the manual from time to time as it deems appropriate, in its sole and
absolute discretion. These provisions supersede all existing policies and practices and may not be
amended or added to without the express written approval of the official legal representative(s) of The
Company.
The only exception to any changes is our employment-at-will policy permitting employees or The
Company to end our relationship for any reason at any time. Employees will be notified of changes to the
manual as they occur.

Core Values

Nothing’s Impossible

Work Hard, Have Fun

We Speak Up

Own the Outcome

Win Together

Our Culture
The Company's brand of culture is a direct reflection of The Company's identity and image, and
our deeply held core values of integrity, respect, trust, teamwork, and excellence. Employees
will notice our culture emerging in the way we treat our Employees, customers, and the
community.
We believe that the collective experience of all Employees is far superior to the individual
knowledge of any one person. The result is a company where Employees depend on each other
to be successful. We focus on teamwork, a hallmark of our culture that extends beyond our own
Employees to our customers, suppliers, and vendors around the country.
We expect our Employees to act with honesty and integrity with themselves and with one
another. As part of this emphasis, we promote an atmosphere where feedback is encouraged
and happens often. Brand building and culture are linked at The Company’s core values. With
our unique culture, we speak to The Brand's enduring values and relevance — creating and
cultivating a greater presence for The Company. Please reference the Integrity Guide for
additional policies and behaviors that would impact employment

Work Policies & Regulations

At-Will Employment
Employment with The Company is voluntarily entered into, and the Employee is free to resign at
will any time, with or without cause. The Company may terminate the employment relationship

at will at any time, with or without notice or cause, so long as there is no violation of applicable
federal or state law.
Policies set forth in this manual are not intended to create a contract, nor are they to be
construed to constitute contractual obligations of any kind or a contract of employment
between The Company and any of its Employees. Employment contracts must be in writing,
limited to a specified period of time and can only be created by the approved legal
representative(s) of The Company.

Equal Employment Opportunity
The Company is committed to equal employment opportunity and implements a policy of
nondiscrimination and affirmative action. The Company will recruit, interview, hire, classify,
select for training, promote, demote, discipline, transfer, adjust rates of pay and terminate on
the basis of merit and qualification without regard to race, religion, creed, color, nationality,
physical disability, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran’s status or any other characteristic
covered by law.
Any Employee determined to have violated this policy in any respect will be subject to
immediate discipline, up to and including termination. The Company complies with applicable
state, local and federal laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. Equal employment
opportunity notices are posted in appropriate areas required by law.
Anyone who believes this policy has been violated may report this violation to the Human
Resources Department.

Open Door Policy
Every Employee is encouraged to open up to their managers about their ideas, perspectives or
feedback. In return, the managers are expected to not only make themselves available but also
foster an environment where Employees’ ideas are welcomed, and their issues are resolved
quickly. Both Parties are expected to foster an environment of trust and mutual respect to
enhance individual performance, team collaboration, and success.
The policy also extends to Human Resources. Employees should contact HR if they have any
questions or concerns about their workplace. There will be no adverse effects based on
comments or concerns that are raised.

Immigration Law Compliance
The Company is committed to employing only United States citizens and aliens who are
authorized to work in the United States and does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of
citizenship or national origin.
In compliance with the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986, each newly hired or
rehired Employee, as a condition of employment, must complete the Employment Eligibility
Verification Form I-9 and present documentation establishing identity and employment
eligibility.

Employees with questions or seeking more information on immigration law issues are
encouraged to contact Human Resources. Employees may raise questions or complaints about
immigration law compliance without fear of reprisal.

Employees may raise questions or complaints about
immigration law compliance without fear of reprisal.

Disability Accommodation-Americans with Disability Act
The Company is committed to complying fully with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and
ensuring equal opportunity in employment for all qualified persons with disabilities. All
employment practices and activities are conducted on a non-discriminatory basis. Reasonable accommodation is available to all disabled employees, where their disability affects
the performance of job functions. All employment decisions are based on the merits of the
situation in accordance with defined criteria, not the disability of the individual. The Act and
final regulations offer protection to individuals who previously had not been considered to be
disabled. Under the ADA, an Employee is disabled if they can establish one of three criteria, he
or she:
o Has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more of the major life
activities of such an individual. o Has a record of such impairment; or
o is regarded as having such impairment. The final regulation greatly expands the meaning of, (but provide only guidelines for)
“substantially limits” and “major life activities”. An employee can have an impairment that is
completely controlled through medication and not actually have any limitation on life activities. However, the employee may still be deemed disabled under ADA. Additionally, impairments
may now be of short duration, intermittent, or episodic and still qualify for disability
It is the employee’s responsibility to inform HR (please see reference list) of any need for an
accommodation.

Upon doing so, The Company may ask for input or the type of accommodation
believed may be necessary, or the function limitations caused by a medical condition. When
appropriate, The Company may need permission to obtain additional information from a
physician or other medial or rehabilitation professionals.

Sexual and Other Forms of Harassment
The Company prohibits dissimilar and unfair treatment of any Employee or individual because of
his/her race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, mental or physical disability, marital status,
veteran status, sexual orientation, family relations, injured worker status or any other status
prohibited by law. This includes harassment and intimidation. Harassment is behavior perceived
by the receiver as unwelcome and includes, but not limited to; the use of verbal or practical
jokes, unwelcome touching, offensive remarks or put-downs, displays of objects, or other
materials which create an offensive work environment.
Harassment may take many forms, including, but not limited to:

chunks.locator: Page 11 — Drug, Alcohol and Smoking Policy
chunks.content:
Drug, Alcohol and Smoking Policy
In compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988, The Company has a longstanding
commitment to provide a safe, quality-oriented, and productive work environment. Alcohol and
drug abuse pose a threat to the health and safety of Company Employees and to the security of
The Company's equipment and facilities. For these reasons, The Company is committed to the
elimination of drug and alcohol use and abuse in the workplace. The possession, use, sale, manufacture or distribution of alcohol, illegal drugs or controlled
substances on company time or on company premises is strictly prohibited. Reporting to work at
any time under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs or controlled substances is strictly
prohibited. With this goal in mind, we are establishing the following policy for all Employees of The
Company. The Company explicitly prohibits:
o The use, possession, solicitation for, or sale of narcotics or other illegal drugs, alcohol, or
prescription medication without a prescription on Company premises or while performing a
work-related assignment. o Being impaired or under the influence of illegal drugs or alcohol on Company premises or on
a work-related assignment. o Possession, use, manufacture, solicitation for, or sale of illegal drugs or alcohol on Company
premises or on a work-related assignment. o The presence of any detectable number of prohibited substances in the Employee's system
while at work or while on Company premises.

Prescribed Medications
o Employees must report to work fit for duty and free of any adverse effects of prescribed
medications.
o This policy does not prohibit Employees from the lawful use and possession of prescribed
medications; however, Employees must consult with their doctors about the medications'
effect on their fitness for duty and ability to work safely, and they must promptly disclose
any work restrictions to the Human Resources Department.
o The Company will not allow Employees to perform their duties while taking prescribed drugs
that are adversely affecting their ability to perform their job duties safely and effectively.
o Employees taking a prescribed medication(s) that may affect their ability to safely and
effectively perform their job duties must carry it in a container labeled by a licensed
pharmacist or be prepared to produce the container if asked.

o Any medications that inhibit an Employee’s ability to perform their job duties safely and
effectively must be reported to the Human Resource Department prior to their next working
day for further review and possible job duty modifications (if applicable).

Smoking/Vaping
o Our business is focused on health, and we have several policies affecting the possession and
use of all tobacco products and nicotine products, including but not limited to cigarettes,
vapor cigarettes, and chewing tobacco while working, or while on the premises. o The Company adheres to all federal, state, local rules regarding smoking in the workplace. Smoking or use of “vapor” products are not permitted in any of the locations. All locations,
including but not limited to all facilities and parking areas and company owned or leased
vehicles are smoke and vapor free. Employees who smoke or use “vapor” products shall do
so off the premises, including the parking lots. The Company reserves the right to undertake monitored drug and/or alcohol testing as follows:
o RANDOM TESTING: Employees may be selected at random for drug and/or alcohol testing at
any interval determined by The Company. This test may be monitored/observed when
administered. o FOR-CAUSE TESTING: The Company may ask an Employee to submit to a drug and/or alcohol
test at any time it has reason to believe that the Employee may be under the influence of
drugs or alcohol, including, but not limited to, the following circumstances: evidence of
drugs or alcohol on or about the Employee's person or in the Employee's vicinity; unusual
conduct on the Employee's part that suggests impairment or influence of drugs or alcohol;
negative performance patterns; or excessive and unexplained absenteeism or tardiness. This
test may be monitored/observed when administered.

o POST-ACCIDENT TESTING: Any Employee involved in an on-the-job accident or injury under
circumstances that suggest possible use or influence of drugs or alcohol in the accident or
injury event will be asked to submit to a drug and/or alcohol test. "Involved in an on-the-job
accident or injury" means not only the one who was or could have been injured, but also
any Employee who potentially contributed to the accident or injury event in any way. This
test may be monitored/observed when administered. If an Employee is tested for drugs or alcohol and the results indicate a violation of this policy, or
if an Employee refuses a request to submit to testing under this policy, the Employee will be
subject to immediate termination.

Standards of Conduct
The Company expects Employees to follow rules of conduct that will protect the interests and
safety of all customers, Employees, and The Company.
The following are examples (non-inclusive list) of infractions that may result in disciplinary

Employment with The Company is at the mutual consent of The Company and the employee,
and either party may terminate that relationship at any time, with or without cause.

Disciplinary Action
The Company maintains a procedure to ensure a fair method of appropriate disciplinary action.
Disciplinary Action is a system intended to give employees advance notice, whenever possible,
or concerns with employee conduct or performance. This provides employees an opportunity to
correct any problems that may arise.
The Company typically operates under the system of three write-ups equal termination,
consisting of verbal warning (documented and put in employee file), written warning, final
written warning, and termination. Management has the authority to suspend employee
discounts or privileges as an alternative form of disciplinary action, or in conjunction with any
previously mentioned step of disciplinary action. Management may also forego the
aforementioned steps and skip to written warning or final written warning. Serious offenses
may result in immediate termination. Employment with The Company is based on mutual
consent and both the employee, and The Company have the right to terminate employment as
will, with or without cause or advance notice. The Company may use progressive discipline at its
discretion.

Attendance
It is the responsibility of each employee to know his or her work schedule and to always be on
time. Lack of punctuality or absenteeism has a negative impact on everyone’s schedule and
creates a lack of service for the client. It is the employee’s responsibility to find a co-worker as a
replacement for a scheduled shift if the employee is not able to work that shift (See Shift
Replacement). If an employee is absent from work for more than two days, a doctor’s note is
required upon return to work. Excessive absenteeism will result in termination. No call or no
show for a scheduled shift may result in immediate termination.
o If an employee is going to be tardy or absent, it is mandatory that the employee call and
speak to their direct manager on duty and notify them of the occurrence at least 2 hours
before their scheduled shift unless it is an instance that it is not possible for them to do so.
(Accident, etc.), Employees must contact their Supervisor via direct phone call immediately.
If an employee is unable to reach their Supervisor, the employee should keep calling up the
chain of command until someone answers.
o Texting a manager is not allowed when calling in. Employees must speak with their
manager directly.
o Seminars/Meetings/ Training sessions are considered scheduled shifts. (See
Seminar/Webinar Attendance section)

Late Opening
When an employee assigned to open a location is unable to open the location at the proper
time, the employee must notify the manager as soon as possible. The manager of the salon will
be required to open the salon and work until the person originally assigned arrives, or a
replacement is found. The employee who failed to open will then be required to reimburse The
Company $25.00 via payroll deduction (when applicable and following all state and local
guidelines), for all expenses incurred. Managers or District Managers will be responsible for
offering restitution to affected clients, as well as giving the payroll deduct total to Payroll. *

chunks.locator: Page 15 — Texting as General Work communications
chunks.content:
Texting as General Work communications
Texting is NOT an acceptable form of communication for official work communications such as;
schedule changes, calling off, shift changes, request offs, availability changes, giving two weeks'
notice, complaints, conversations regarding disciplinary or corrective actions, or for any other
topics that may cause a hardship to the business, etc.. These instances require direct
communication either in person or via phone call(s). Texting may be acceptable for other
reasons but check with direct Supervisor(s) regarding when texting may be acceptable.

chunks.locator: Page 15 — Dress Code for The Company
chunks.content:
Dress Code for The Company
The Company Employees are to keep a neat, clean, professional appearance at all times. Anyone
violating their Brand’s Dress code policy will be sent home to change into proper work attire and
may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and potentially including termination.

All Locations Dress Code:
Name tags
o Name tags are to be worn and visible at all times while working.
o Each Employee will receive one name tag.
o Additional or replacement tags can be ordered through a manager at the Employee’s
expense.

Shoes
o Tennis shoes or other full coverage closed toe shoes are to be worn.
o No sandals, crocks, flip-flops, or other open toe shoes are allowed.
o Shoes must be tied at all times and must be clean with no holes.

Belts
o Belts are to be dark brown or black.
o Belts are not to hang down or have objects (cell phones, pagers, chains, keys, etc.) hanging
from them.

Hair
o Hair of all lengths and colors are acceptable as long as it is clean, groomed, and kept out of
employee’s face and eyes.

Facial Hair
o Facial hair is acceptable as long as it is clean, well-groomed, and trimmed.

Make-up
o Due to the nature of working in the Beauty Industry, reasonable and natural make-up is
acceptable and encouraged.

Jewelry/Accessories
o Jewelry that does not interfere with work is acceptable.
o No dangling earrings or chains, and no pins or buttons allowed on the shirt unless approved
by Management.

Tattoos
o Large, inappropriate, or offensive tattoos must be covered. All other tattoos are acceptable
as long as they are not discriminatory or offensive in nature.

All aspects of the dress code are at The Company’s discretion, if an employee has a question, please

Personal Items:
Personal items (books, laptops, other electronics, etc.) do not belong inside The Company,
unless necessary. Employees are expected to tend to company business while at work, not their
own business. The Company assumes no risk or liability for any theft or damage that may occur
to Employee property while it is on company property.

Employee Parking
Employees are not allowed to park directly in front of the location. Parking spaces closest to the
front of the location are to be reserved for customers. The Company assumes no risk or liability
for any theft or damage that may occur to Employee vehicles or the contents of Employee
vehicles while they are on company property.

Lost and Found
All Employees are responsible for securing lost and found items.
o Follow these instructions when an employee locates lost and found items:
▪ Place the item in an envelope with the Lost and Found Tracker form stapled to the
outside OR place the item in a clear Ziploc bag with this form inside.
▪ Fill out the Lost and Found Tracker form and follow up properly until the customer
has picked up the item.
▪ All items worth 50 dollars or more should be kept in the drop safe (this includes;
jewelry, cellphones, etc.) All items worth less than 50 dollars should be kept in a box
(socks, hats, shirts, eyewear, etc.)
▪ Notify managers if a customer has not picked up the item within 60 days.
o If an item is found by an Employee, it is their legal responsibility to return it to the rightful
owner. Deviations from this policy will not be tolerated. Items found must be returned to
the customer or criminal suits may follow.

Facility Repair/Service Vendors
Whenever a contracted repair/service vendor enters the workplace to fix a facility issue or
provide services other than the normal monthly scheduled work such as rug replacement,
window cleaning, etc., the employee must immediately contact the location manager on duty
PRIOR to letting them complete any work or access any facilities or systems. If there are no
members of Management present, call up the chain of command until one is reached.
To protect company Employees, customers, our data and facilities, employees must receive the
approval of a member of Management, who should confirm the repair was requested and
expected, before employees allow the repair vendor to do any work or to access any of our
facilities or systems. Failure to get approval/access permission prior to allowing a repair or
service vendor to access our systems or facilities may result in disciplinary action, up to and
including immediate termination as allowing potential unauthorized access puts our entire
company, Employees, and customers at risk.

Purchasing Authorizations
Employees do not have authority to verbally represent or sign anything, other than acceptance
of normal business deliveries and regularly scheduled routine services, on behalf of The

Company, unless given prior approval in writing by Upper Management, official company
directive, or the legal department. Employees are prohibited from signing any contracts or legal
agreements on behalf of The Company, without specific approval of the Owner. Employees are
prohibited from purchasing any products, supplies, or services for use at any company location
without express written approval from Upper Management, regardless of whether or not the
Employee expects to receive reimbursement for the expense.

Discounting
The only discounting allowed by The Company is in conjunction with a pre-approved
promotional offer. A coupon must accompany the applied discount unless specified otherwise
by Management or company communications regarding approved discount offers.
The only use of the manual discount/price override function by non-Management personnel
should be for Employee purchases. Only members of Management are allowed to give manual
discounts/price overrides for transactions other than Employee purchases. Employee purchases
must be processed on the Employee’s account. Any deviation from this policy will result in
immediate termination.

Coupon Collection
Anytime employees collect a promotional coupon from a customer, the following steps must be
taken:
o Printed Coupons – Collect the coupon from the customer.
o Non-Printed Coupons – For example: Coupons shown from a cell phone -
▪ Print the receipt after the transaction is processed. Write the promotional offer the
customer has shown using their phone on a receipt. The receipt in turn becomes
their coupon.
o Write employee name, the customer's name, the customer number, the date, and “VOID”
across the coupon.
o Include all coupons with nightly deposit at the end of the shift.

Cell Phone/Smart Watch Policy
Personal Employee cell phones are permitted in the workplace but must be kept out of sight. It
is the Employee’s personal responsibility to protect the customer’s experience and doing things
such as texting, making phone calls or using social media jeopardizes the customer’s experience.
Employees should keep cell phones on silent and not on their person (this means not in back
pockets, charging in the break room, or sitting on top of a drawer till). The only time that a cell
phone should be accessed while clocked in is in emergency situations.
Smart Watches are allowed as long as they are not being used for social media or texting/phone
calls. We reserve the right to ask Employees to remove any smart watch if it starts to interfere
with the customer's experience.

Company Email Account
Only authorized Employees may access their company email and may not use their company
email for personal use.

Point of Sale and Alarm Passwords
Employees must always use their own personal passwords and alarm codes. Do NOT share
alarm codes or passwords. Using the password or alarm code of another Employee or giving
another Employee individual passwords or alarm codes, for any reason, is a violation of policy
and may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

Employment Verification
Employment verification, both current and previous, is to be handled by the Corporate Office. If
employees are asked to verify or comment on any aspect of an Employee’s current or past
history with The Company, employees are to refer the inquiry to the Corporate Office with
Human Resources.

Outside Employment
The Company requires that any outside employment not compromise the company’s interests,
adversely affect the employee’s job performance and ability to fulfill all responsibilities to the
company or create a liability for the company. Working for a direct competitor is strictly
prohibited.
Managers are strictly prohibited from working another job. It is the manager's responsibility to
be available at all times to tend to the business of the location. Managers are allowed to attend
school; however, all class schedules must be approved in advance by the District Manager and
are expected to not interfere with the Manager’s availability.

Fraternization Policy
All Employees are strongly discouraged from dating other Employees. Anyone in a Supervisory
position is prohibited from dating a subordinate, without Management Team approval. Personal
relationships between Employees should not unfavorably impact either Employee’s morale or
the effectiveness of company operations. Employees who are considering possibly engaging in a
personal relationship that would result in potential violations of this policy must contact Human
Resources. Deviation from this policy will result in immediate termination.

chunks.locator: Page 20 — Employment and Supervision of Relatives
chunks.content:
Employment and Supervision of Relatives
The Company discourages the employment or transfer of relatives to any position where a
family member supervises (or acts in a supervisory capacity to) another family member.
Selection, assignment, and review of every employee should be as objective as possible. When
family is involved, it is difficult to be objective and almost impossible to appear objective. All
familial relationships within locations must have prior approval by Human Resources.

Solicitation
Persons not employed by The Company may not solicit or distribute literature in the workplace
at any time. Employees may not solicit or distribute literature concerning activities during
working time. (Working time does not include lunch periods, work breaks, or any other periods
in which Employees are not on duty). Posting of written solicitations on The Company bulletin
boards is restricted. These bulletin boards display important information, and Employees should
consult the bulletin boards frequently. If Employees have a message of interest to the

workplace, they must submit it to Management for approval. The Manager will post all
approved messages.

Care and Cleaning of Equipment and Facilities
All Employees must do their best to keep the equipment and the workplace clean at all times. It
is the responsibility of every employee to ensure completion of appropriate checklists are
completed each shift.

No Public Restrooms
The Company restrooms are for paying customers and Employees only. The Company does not
provide public restrooms.

Location Closing Times
The Company accepts customers until the posted closing time. Failure to accept customers up
to the posted closing time will result in immediate disciplinary action.

Background Checks
Employees are subject to background checks for certain positions and promotions. The
background check form will be completed and submitted to Human Resources.

Business Ethics
The Company strives to maintain a reputation for honesty and integrity in the marketplace. All
Company Employees will conduct themselves with the utmost integrity in all dealings with
customers, vendors, and fellow Employees.
Please reference the JB & Associates Integrity Guide for more helpful guidance and information
on this topic.

Communication and Confidentiality Policies

Confidential Information Policy
All Company data and information is the property of The Company and is intended for company
use only. This data and information include, but is not limited to:
o Any and all financial information
o Employee and customer data
o Marketing strategies
o Vendors
o Pending legal matters
All departments have information that must be kept confidential at all times. Employees are
responsible for monitoring and protecting all confidential information. Each department
Employee must follow all guidelines to ensure confidential information is handled properly. All
Employees are required to utilize encrypted passwords for all company related logins.
o An encrypted password is more secure than password protection. It makes passwords
unreadable and/or unusable by hackers.
o Requirements:

▪ Do not use a word or phrase of special importance to you, i.e., birthday, place, or
vehicle.
▪ Do not use default passwords, i.e., password123.
▪ The password should be 8-10 characters long.
▪ Include numbers.
▪ Include special characters, i.e., */&$#@.
▪ Include at least one capital letter and one lower case letter.
Examples of ways to keep information confidential can include, but are not limited to:
o Shredding of financial documents
o Using screen saver passwords
To protect employee privacy, no aspect of employment outside of what is required to complete
legal employment verifications and to process required aspects such as; processing payroll,
managing employment benefits, etc. will be discussed with any outside parties without
employee consent.

Nondisclosure Agreement Policy
A nondisclosure agreement is a legally enforceable contract that creates a confidential
relationship to protect sensitive information. By signing a nondisclosure agreement, participants
promise to not divulge, or release information shared with them by the other people involved.
If the information is leaked, the injured person can claim breach of contract.
If an employee of The Company, is asked to sign a nondisclosure agreement by a customer or an
outside vendor, do not sign anything and immediately contact a direct Supervisor.

Talking to the Media/Press
Any conversation with the media or press, including television stations, radio stations,
newspapers, etc., is strictly prohibited. Please direct any and all media inquiries to the
Corporate Office.

Social Media Policy
The Company understands that social media can be a fun and rewarding way to share an
employee’s life and opinions with family, friends, and co-workers around the world. Social
media includes all means of communicating, posting information, or content of any sort on the
internet. This may come from; employee’s own or someone else’s web log or blog, journal or
diary, personal website, social networking or affinity website, web bulletin board or a chat
room, as well as many other forms of electronic communication whether it is associated with
The Company or not.

Guidelines
Inappropriate postings that may include discriminatory remarks, harassment, and threats of
violence, or similar inappropriate or unlawful conduct, will not be tolerated and may subject an
employee to disciplinary action up to and including termination. Employees should avoid using
statements, photographs, video, or audio that reasonably could be viewed as malicious,
obscene, threatening or intimidating, that disparage customers, Employees or suppliers, or that
might constitute harassment or bullying (see the section on Harassment).

Employees should be honest and accurate when posting information or news, if an employee
make a mistake, correct it quickly. Maintain the confidentiality of The Company’s trade secrets
and private or confidential information. Do not post internal reports, policies, procedures, or
other internal business-related confidential communications. Do not create a link to an
employee blog, website, or other social networking/media site to The Company website without
identifying yourself as a company Employee.

chunks.locator: Page 23 — Using Social Media at Work
chunks.content:
Using Social Media at Work
Avoid using social media while on work time or on equipment we provide unless it is work-
related as authorized by your supervisor or consistent with Company policy. Do not use
Company email addresses to register on social networks, blogs or other online tools utilized for
personal use.

Retaliation is Prohibited
The Company prohibits taking negative action against any Employee for reporting a possible
deviation from any policy or for cooperating in an investigation. Any Employee who retaliates
against another Employee for reporting a possible deviation from any policy or for cooperating
in an investigation will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination. If
employees have a question or need further guidance, please contact Human Resources.

Company assets include anything owned or leased by The Company for operational and business
use, to include (but is not limited to) systems, data, computers, personal devices, applications,
facilities, connections, individuals, documentation, and electronic media, whether located on
The Company’s premise or off-site, and all Company locations where cardholder data is present. All users are required to follow the Information Security Policy at all times, unless a prior
exception request has been reviewed and approved by a member of The Company’s Senior
Management Team. This policy is distributed to all users granted access to any Company asset, to include Company
Employees, third-parties, service providers, contractors, temporary Employees, and/or other
staff members. Managers, Employees, and technical personnel must modify system
configurations and procedures, if necessary to comply with the terms of this policy as promptly
as possible, with the goal of doing so within ten (10) business days following adoption or
amendment. o Disclaimer of Liability: The Company is not responsible for material viewed or downloaded
by users from the internet. Users are cautioned that many of these pages include offensive,
sexually explicit, and inappropriate material. Even innocuous search requests may lead to
sites with highly offensive content. In addition, having an email address on the internet may
lead to the receipt of unsolicited emails containing offensive content. Users accessing the
internet do so at their own risk.

Communications Systems Policy
Telephones, mail systems, computers, internet access, email, and etc. provided by The Company
are company property and may be accessed by The Company in the ordinary course of business.
Employees should have no expectation of privacy in the information contained in voicemail or
computers. Employees have no proprietary interest in any voicemail or email and The Company
reserves the right to monitor, listen to, view, copy, disclose or delete any telephone
conversations, voicemails or emails, including blogging, at any time.
Installation of either unauthorized software or hardware on any of our computer systems is
strictly prohibited. It is expected that there will be times when it is necessary to either make or
receive personal telephone calls. Personal use of The Company-provided telephone for long-
distance and toll calls is not permitted. You may be required to reimburse The Company for any
charges resulting from personal use of the telephone or if you incur additional fee services
charges.

Information Technology Support
Technology use at The Company continues to grow rapidly. A variety of hardware and software
is being used by a diverse group of people to achieve a variety of goals. The Information

abilities.

Safety in the Workplace

Security Policy
The Company is committed to the safety and security of our customers, Employees, and other
company assets. To that end, all staff must remain vigilant for any type of situation(s),
person(s), or device(s) that could pose a threat of any type in any way and should report any
concerns immediately as appropriate. All Employees must also complete all required actions
regarding safety and safety checks as stipulated in your brand’s training and operations
manuals.

chunks.section: Statement of Safety in the Workplace Policy
chunks.content:
Statement of Safety in the Workplace Policy
Our Employees are our most valuable assets. It is our policy that every person is entitled to a
safe and have a healthful place in which to work. Establishment and maintenance of a safe
environment is the shared responsibility between the employer and Employees at all levels of
The Company. To this end, every reasonable effort will be made in achieving the goal of
accident prevention and health preservation. Our philosophy is oriented toward affirmative control and minimization of risk to the greatest
extent possible. We have a basic responsibility to make the safety of Employees a part of our
concern. We will be counting on you to do your part in making our program an effective one. The success of The Company will depend not only on production and sales, but also how safely
each job is performed. There is neither a job so important nor any service so urgent that we
cannot take time to work safely. The Company will aggressively pursue a plan to minimize pain and suffering of an injured worker
and return him/her to active work duties as soon as possible. We consider the safety of our
personnel to be of prime importance, and we expect your full cooperation in our program
effective. Employee Notice: All Employees must promptly report any occupational injury or illness to their
Supervisor. If a Supervisor is not present, the report must be made to any on-site member of
Management.

the Employee obtains or receives prompt medical attention as needed. The Supervisor will document the incident as required by state and federal safety regulations,
and Upper Management will initiate an investigation as to the cause of the incident. Employees,

To report a work-related injury or illness or to request copies of occupational injury and illness
record, please contact: Your Supervisor or a member of Management in your chain of
command. You may also contact Human Resources.

Emergency Situation Notification Requirement
Anytime emergency personnel are called (other than for false alarms), or an injury requiring
medical treatment occurs, employees are required to call their Supervisor immediately.
Employees must leave a voicemail if the call is not answered, then continue calling up the chain
of command until someone is reached. They will provide you with additional instructions
and/or directions. For severe events, the District Manager/Regional Manager or similar upper-
level Manager, and Human Resources should be notified.
Emergencies such as severe weather, power failures, etc., can disrupt company operations. In
extreme cases, these circumstances may require the closing of a brand location or office. The
Corporate Office Personnel will advise the Supervisors if a brand location or office will be closing
or should remain closed. When operations are officially closed due to emergency conditions, per
FLSA requirements, time off from scheduled work will be paid for all salary exempt Employees
regardless of the duration of the closing, however hourly non-exempt Employees will not be
paid for any scheduled work hours during the closed time frame. With Supervisory approval,
hourly non-exempt Employees may use available paid leave time (PTO) to be compensated for
scheduled work time that will be unpaid due to emergency closings.

Incident Reporting
Any incident including theft, burglary, property damage, robbery, suspicious/inappropriate
behavior, severe weather event resulting in any type of business interruption, late-opening,
unplanned closing, or injury must be documented in an incident report. Details of the incident
must be submitted to employee’s Supervisor immediately for any situation that requires
immediate emergency response or medical attention. Once all details are obtained, the
Supervisor, depending on brand/department’s specified operational procedures will create a
computer-generated incident report.

Post Investigation Consequences:
When incidents requiring an investigation occur, if the investigation findings determine that the
cause of the incident was due to specific Employee(s) carelessness, willful disregard of safety
protocols, negligence, or other conduct prohibited per the Standards of Conduct policy, the
Employee(s) found to be at fault will be held accountable and may receive disciplinary action up
to and possibly including transfer, suspension with or without pay, demotion, or immediate
termination of employment, as well as potential civil or criminal prosecution depending on the
severity and details of the circumstances involved.

chunks.section: Employee Injury/Illness in the Workplace & Related Accommodations
chunks.content:
Employee Injury/Illness in the Workplace & Related Accommodations:

Following any work-related injury or illness, regardless of severity, it is the Employee’s
responsibility to report the injury/illness immediately to their Supervisor so they can provide
prompt and trained evaluation and obtain medical attention if necessary and for completion of
an incident report. If the condition reasonably precludes immediate notice, the injury should be
reported as soon as possible. No Employee will perform First Aid on a co-worker unless they
have been trained to do so. If you are unable to perform First Aid on your own injury, notify
your Supervisor. They will direct you to where to seek medical treatment.
Employees are personally responsible for returning their medical reports, restrictions, or any
required time off of work to their direct Supervisor within 24 hours of their medical review.
Once medical documentation is obtained, The Company will work to get the Employee back to
work as quickly and as safely as possible.

chunks.content:
Employee Non-Work-Related Injury/Illness Accommodations
When a potential new hire or current Employee is stating they have work restrictions or when
The Company determines that the Employee is unable to fulfill their work duties in an
acceptable manner due to a non-work-related injury or illness, the Employee must provide
medical documentation from their physician stating the specific restrictions based on the Job
Function Evaluation form provided by their Supervisor. Once this documentation is obtained, it
should be immediately submitted to the Corporate Office/Human Resources who will review the
documents and determine if reasonable accommodations can be made for the Employee.
If reasonable accommodations are not possible, the Employee must follow the standard
FMLA/STD procedure to see if they qualify. If reasonable accommodations can be made, a
“Reasonable Accommodation Agreement” document will be sent for both the Employee and
Supervisor to sign, indicating their agreement to follow and abide by the accommodations as
listed.

Problem Resolution
The Company encourages an open and honest atmosphere in which any problem, complaint,
suggestion, or question receives a timely response from The Company Supervisors and
Management. Supervisors, location managers, and Employees are expected to treat each other
with mutual respect. Employees are encouraged to offer positive and constructive feedback. If
Employees disagree with established rules of conduct, policies, or practices, they can express
their concern through the problem resolution procedure. No Employee will be penalized for
voicing a complaint with The Company in a reasonable, businesslike manner, or for using the
problem resolution procedure.
If a situation occurs in which Employees believe that a condition of employment or a decision
affecting them is unjust or inequitable, they are encouraged to make use of the following steps.
The Employee may discontinue the procedure at any step.
o An Employee presents a problem to their immediate Supervisor within 7 calendar days, or
as soon as reasonably possible after an incident occurs. If a Supervisor is unavailable or the
Employee believes it would be inappropriate to contact that person, the Employee may
present the problem to the next member of Management above their Supervisor in the
chain of command.

o The Supervisor responds to the problem during a discussion or within 7 calendar days, or as
soon as reasonably possible after consulting with appropriate Management members, when
necessary. The Supervisor documents the discussion.
o If the problem is unresolved, the Employee will present the problem to the next member of
Management above their Supervisor in the chain of command within 7 calendar days, or as
soon as reasonably possible.
o That manager will review and consider the problem and inform the Employee of a decision
within 7 calendar days, or as soon as reasonably possible.
o If the problem is unresolved, the Employee will present the problem to Human Resources
within 7 calendar days, or as soon as reasonably possible.
o Human Resources has full authority to make any adjustments deemed appropriate to
resolve the problem.
Not every problem can be resolved to everyone's total satisfaction, but only through
understanding and discussion of mutual problems can Employees and Management develop
confidence in each other.

Workplace Violence Prevention
The Company has adopted the following guidelines to deal with intimidation, harassment, or
other threats of (or actual) violence that may occur during business hours or on its premises. All Employees, including Supervisors and temporary Employees, should be treated with courtesy
and respect at all times. Employees are expected to refrain from fighting, “horseplay”, or other
conduct that may be dangerous to others. Firearms, weapons, and other dangerous or
hazardous devices or substances are prohibited from the premises of The Company without
proper authorization. Conduct that threatens, intimidates, or coerces another Employee, a customer of the public at
any time, including off-duty periods, will not be tolerated. This prohibition includes all acts of
harassment, including harassment that is based on an individual’s race, religion, creed, color,
nationality, physical disability, sex, age, veteran’s status, or any other characteristic covered by
law. All threats of (or actual) violence, both direct and indirect, should be reported as soon as
possible to your immediate Supervisor or any other member of Management. This includes
threats by Employees, as well as threats by customers, vendors, solicitors, or other members of
the public. When reporting a threat of violence, you should be as specific and detailed as
possible. All suspicious individuals or activities should also be reported as soon as possible to a
Supervisor. Do not place yourself in a dangerous situation.

All suspicious individuals or activities should also be reported as soon as possible to a
Supervisor. Do not place yourself in a dangerous situation.

If you see or hear a commotion or
disturbance near your workstation, do not try to intercede. The Company will promptly and thoroughly investigate all reports of threats of (or actual)
violence and of suspicious individuals or activities. The identity of the individual making the
report will be protected as much as it is practical. To maintain workplace safety and the
integrity of its investigation, The Company may suspend Employees, either with or without pay,
pending investigation.

Anyone determined to be responsible for threats of (or actual) violence or other conduct that is
in violation of these guidelines will be subject to prompt disciplinary action up to and including
immediate termination.
The Company encourages Employees to bring their disputes or differences with other
Employees to the attention of their Supervisors before the situation escalates into potential
violence. The Company will not discipline Employees for raising such concerns.

Visitors in the Workplace
This policy applies to The Company. Visitors include all persons who are granted access to
Company premises, including, but not limited to, Employees, contractors, customers, and
Employees’ acquaintances, friends and family members, regardless of whether the purpose of
the visit is for business reasons. For personal visitors, Employees must obtain approval from direct Supervisors each time they
invite a visitor into the workplace. The Supervisor has responsibility for enforcing this policy and
ensuring that visitors (regardless of whether or not they are JB & Associates Employees) stay for
only limited and non-disruptive periods of time. If a visitor does not have approval and/or is
unannounced, the Supervisor will verify with the Employee that the visitor is “welcome”. If the
visitor is welcome, the Employee will be asked to meet the visitor at the front
entrance/reception area. If the Employee is uncomfortable with allowing the visitor into the
workplace, the Supervisor or manager on duty must refuse to allow the visitor into the
workplace. Violent domestic issues, including Restraining Orders, PPO-Personal Protection Orders, and
intense domestic concerns should be communicated promptly to Human Resources and the
direct Supervisor to promote a safe and secure workplace. Employees who have invited guests are responsible for escorting non-Employee visitors to their
destinations and always accompanying them. Employees are responsible for the conduct of their
visitors.

Employees are responsible for the conduct of their
visitors.

Upon observing an unescorted non-Employee visitor or a visitor (Employee or non-
Employee) acting inappropriately on Company premises, Employees must immediately notify
Management. Visitors should be aware that unauthorized animals are not permitted in areas
within the workplace, including parking lots. Employees who are not scheduled to be working should not be in the workplace unless they are
shopping or receiving services from the workplace. Employees must promptly report to a Supervisor, suspicious vehicles, individual, threatening
calls, situations of workplace violence, or even domestic violence if that might impact this or any
company properties. Such reports are kept strictly confidential, and there will be no adverse
effects based on you are an Employee’s reported comments or concerns. Do not place yourself
in a dangerous situation. If you see or hear a commotion or disturbance near your workstation,
contact your Supervisor. Do not try to intercede. The Company will promptly and thoroughly
investigate all reports of threats of (or actual) violence and of suspicious individuals or activities. ONLY employees are allowed behind the front counter/cash register area, in kitchen areas, or
other back-room production areas used for storage if they are working their current shift.

Animals in the Workplace
The Company is responsible for assuring the health and safety of all Employees in the
workplace. While we understand that people dearly love their pets and like to take them
everywhere, the fact is that animals may:
o Pose a threat of infection
o Cause allergic reactions in other Employees/customers
o Cause some Employees/customers to feel threatened or to be distracted by the
presence of animals
o “Have accidents” or damage to company property
Therefore, in consideration of all Employees and to ensure safety, please do not bring pets into
the workplace. An Employee who requires the help of a service animal (defined by 28 CFR
36.104 as “any dog that is individually trained to do work or perform tasks for the benefit of an
individual with a disability”) will be permitted to bring a service animal to the office, provided
that the animal’s presence does not create a danger to others and does not impose an undue
hardship upon The Company.

Robberies
Robberies are rare situations that may occur. Robberies involve a person or persons forcing an
Employee to give him or her cash, merchandise, etc. It is best practice to be proactive before
these situations occur. By following all safety policies, we can minimize the opportunity for the
crime. Robberies can occur inside or outside any company location, etc. In the case of a robbery,
give any robber whatever items/cash they demand. Do not in anyway attempt to foil the
robbery, negotiate, or battle wits with a potential robber(s).
The safety of our Employees, outside vendors, guests, and reputation cannot be risked for any
monetary value. Immediately contact the local authorities and your immediate Supervisor and
follow Emergency Situation Notification Requirement policy if this situation occurs. An Incident
Form must be completed and submitted. Your Supervisor will instruct you on how to complete
this form. (See also Incident Reporting).

Handling Theft
The Company Employees who have witnessed or suspect an act of dishonesty or business
abuses should report it to the manager on duty, District Manager, or other Upper Management.
o It is paramount that employees do not discuss suspicions to anyone else in The Company, or
outside of work.
Employees should not act on their own to resolve the theft issue. Communicate concerns as
outlined above. We must prevent theft at all times to secure the success of our company. Theft
is a loss that can be prevented. Following the correct procedures above will ensure that theft is
avoided and handled lawfully and ethically when it does occur.
