chunks.locator: Page 31 — Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines
chunks.section: Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines
chunks.content:
Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines
The purpose of this policy is to promote the safety of those individuals who drive company
vehicles or who drive personal vehicles for business use, and to provide guidance on the proper
use of vehicles for company business. It is the driver’s responsibility to operate the vehicle in a
safe manner and to drive defensively to prevent injuries and property damage. As such, The
Company endorses and requires your compliance with all applicable state motor vehicle
regulations relating to driver responsibility. In addition, The Company expects each driver to
drive in a safe and courteous manner pursuant to the following safety rules:
Company vehicles are to be driven by authorized Employees only, except in case of repair
testing by a mechanic. Employees must have a valid and current Driver’s License to operate a
company vehicle, or a personal vehicle with current auto insurance while on company business.
Any Employee who has a Driver’s License revoked or suspended shall immediately notify Human
Resources by 9 a.m. central time the next business day, and immediately discontinue operation
of The Company vehicle. Failure to do so may result in disciplinary action, up to and including
termination of employment.
All accidents that occur involving company vehicles, or personal vehicles while being driven for
company business, and involving personal injury, regardless of severity, must be reported to the
police and to Human Resources. Drivers must report all ticketed traffic violations received

sections.heading: Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines

chunks.locator: Page 32 — Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines
chunks.section: Vehicle Fleet Usage Policy and Guidelines
chunks.content:
during the operation of a company vehicle, or while driving a personal vehicle on company
business, within 72 hours to Human Resources.
A driving record that fails to meet criteria stated in this policy, or that is considered to be in
violation of the intent of this policy, will result in a loss of the privilege of driving a company
vehicle.
Criteria that may indicate an unacceptable record include, but are not limited to:
o Three or more moving violations in a year.
o Three or more chargeable accidents within a year. Chargeable means that they driver is
determined to be the primary cause of the accident through speeding, inattention, etc.
Contributing factors, such as weather or mechanical problems, will be taken into
consideration.
o Violations include any ticket, charge, or other law enforcement proceeding relating to these,
as well as independent evidence of violations deemed credible and relevant by The
Company.

Driver Safety Rules
The use of a company vehicle, or driving a personal vehicle for company business, while under
the influence of intoxicants and other drugs (which could impair driving ability) is forbidden and
is sufficient cause for discipline, up to and including termination of employment.
The Company does not allow or require cell phone use while driving and Employees are
expressly forbidden from texting, responding to email or any other actions that may distract the
Employee from safe driving. Cell phone use while driving should be kept to a minimum and
when done shall only be done in a manner that does not distract the driver.
Drivers are responsible for the security of company vehicles assigned to them. The vehicle
engine must be shut off, ignition keys removed, and vehicle doors locked whenever the vehicle
is left unattended. All State and Local laws must be obeyed.

Accident Procedures
Employees should call for medical aid if necessary. Call the police. All accidents, regardless of
severity, must be reported to the police. If the driver cannot get to a phone, he/she should
write a note giving location to a reliable appearing motorist and ask them to notify the police.
Record names and addresses of driver, witnesses, and occupants of the other vehicles and any
medical personnel who may arrive at the scene. Pertinent information to obtain includes license
number of other drivers; insurance company names and policy numbers of other vehicles; make,
model, and year of other vehicles; date and time of accident; and overall road and weather
conditions.
Do not discuss the accident with anyone at the scene except the police. Do not accept any
responsibility for the accident. Do not argue with anyone. Provide the other party with
employee name, address, Driver’s License number, and insurance information.
Immediately report the accident to Human Resources. Provide a copy of the accident report
and/or your written description of the accident to Human Resources ASAP. There will be a

formal accident review conducted on each accident to determine cause and how the accident
could have been prevented.

Employment Status & Records

Employee Classifications
Company policies apply to all classifications of Employees; however, Employees are divided into
the following classifications:
o Full-time – Employees hired full time (30 hours per week or more) on a full workweek basis
for a continuous and indefinite period of time.
o The following hours are required per position:
o AMM/ASD/AGM – 30-35 hours per week
o Hourly Office Personnel - 40 hours per week
o MM/SD/GM/TSD/DM – 40-45 hours per week
o Part-time – Employees whose work schedule is less than full time (less than 30 hours per
week) on a full workweek basis for a continuous and indefinite period of time.
o Temporary/Seasonal – Employees hired as temporary workers for short periods of time
such as holidays, peak seasonal periods, and vacations. Upon completion of the temporary
assignment, temporary/seasonal Employees should be terminated or reclassified as part-
time or full-time.
o Nonexempt – All nonexempt Employees are paid bi-weekly on an hourly basis and are
expected to confine their work to the scheduled workday and workweek unless their
supervisor authorizes overtime in advance. Hourly paid Employees will be paid overtime for
all hours worked in excess of 40 hours within a workweek. Workweek is defined as opening
business Monday through close of business Sunday.
o Exempt – All exempt Employees are paid on a bi-weekly salary basis. Hours worked by
salaried Employees can be irregular. Salaried Employees are exempt from the overtime
provisions of the Federal Wage and Hour Law and do not receive overtime pay.

Orientation
The Supervisor will discuss job duties and responsibilities with the new Employee once
employment commences. A copy of the Employment Policy Manual will be available in each
location physically or digitally for all Employees to review at any time. The manual is not to be
removed from the salon. Employees are expected to read the manual thoroughly and address
any questions with their supervisor. An Acknowledgement of Receipt and Understanding is
provided in the New Hire Paperwork, which the employee is required to sign. This signed copy
will become part of the employee’s personnel file. Additionally, all employees must present on
their start date, a voided check or a direct deposit form from their bank, along with the
necessary copies of their identification (according to the I-9). If these items are not presented on
the start date, all training will cease until the employee can present the proper documentation.

Introductory Period (Probationary Period)
The introductory period is intended to give new Employees the opportunity to demonstrate
their ability to achieve a satisfactory level of performance and to determine whether the new
position meets their expectations. The Company uses this period to evaluate Employee

capabilities, work habits, and overall performance. Either the Employee or The Company may
end the employment relationship at will, at any time, during or after the introductory period,
with or without cause or advance notice.
All new and rehired Employees work on an introductory basis for the first 90 calendar days after
their date of hire. Employees who are promoted or transferred within The Company must
complete a secondary introductory period of the same length with each reassignment to a new
position. Any significant absence will automatically extend an introductory period by the length
of the absence. If The Company determines that the designated introductory period does not
allow sufficient time to thoroughly evaluate the Employee’s performance, the introductory
period may be extended for a specified period.
In cases of promotions or transfers within The Company, an Employee who, in the sole
judgement of Management, is not successful in the new position can be removed from that
position at any time during the secondary introductory period. If this occurs, the Employee may
be allowed to return to his or her former job or to a comparable job or the Employee is
qualified, depending on the availability of such positions and The Company’s needs.

Evaluations and Raises
Employees are entitled to a review and potential raises at least annually. The Company cannot
promise or guarantee that raises will occur as raises are based upon several factors including but
not limited to: Employee performance, location performance, and overall company
performance.

Promotions
The Company is eager to promote from within and values employee growth and development.
Qualified Employees are encouraged to apply for internal job postings. When we have an
Employee who is fully qualified and willing to perform the duties of the available position, which
may include relocating. Promotions will be based on quality of work, prior job performance,
experience and willingness to relocate. Questions regarding job openings and the internal
application process should be directed to Human Resources.

chunks.locator: Page 34 — What to Expect When Terminated
chunks.content:
What to Expect When Terminated

Employment Termination
Below are examples of some most common circumstances which employment is terminated:
o Resignation – voluntary employment termination initiated by an Employee. The Company
requests that you discuss a notice period with your immediate Supervisor(s). If an Employee
does not provide advance notice, the Employee will be ineligible for rehire.
o Discharge – involuntary employment termination initiated by The Company.
o Layoff – involuntary employment termination initiated by The Company for non-disciplinary
reasons.
o Retirement – voluntary employment termination initiated by the Employee meeting age,
length of service, and any other criteria for retirement from The Company.

Return of Property
Employees must return all company property immediately upon request and no later than 5 pm
the following business day upon termination of employment. Ex: laptops/tablets, cellphones,
uniforms, company vehicle, keys, key fobs, company credit cards and all corresponding receipts
or invoices, company paperwork, expense reports and receipts, tools, equipment, company
manuals, company training items/devices, and any other company issued property or assets,
etc..
When permitted by applicable law, The Company may also take all legal action deemed
appropriate to recover or protect its property and its return including criminal and civil charges.
Employees may be held financially responsible for damaged or unreturned property and The
Company reserves the right to withhold the cost of repairing or replacing such property from
the Employee’s paycheck(s) where allowed by law.
As an Employee you have the right to request a receipt from your Supervisor showing items you
returned (typically through email).

chunks.locator: Page 35 — Pay on Separation of Employment
chunks.content:
Pay on Separation of Employment
Upon separation of employment, Employees will be paid for time worked, less deductions, on
the next regular pay day. In most instances, the final paycheck will be mailed or direct deposited
to the Employee from the Corporate Office.
A two (2) week notice is required for all full time and part-time Employees, and a thirty (30) day
notice is required for all Management positions. If employees do not fulfill the required notice,
hourly Employees will be reduced to minimum wage and lose all bonus potential, within the
rules and regulations of the Fair Labor Standard Act.
You must fulfill your notice to receive any bonuses that have not yet been paid out. No bonuses
will be paid upon involuntary termination of employment. All Employee discounts for items and
services will cease immediately upon separation of employment.

Employee Records
The Company will maintain a file on each Employee. Personnel files are the property of The
Company and will be treated as any other confidential information. All personnel files are kept
in the Personnel Platform Systems via the systems below or at the Corporate Office:
o Sun Tan City – MyGlow
o Buff City Soap – MyGlow
o Crunch Fitness – Woven
It is the responsibility of each employee to promptly notify The Company of any changes in
personnel data. Personal mailing addresses, telephone numbers, number and names of
dependents, individuals to be contacted in the event of an emergency, educational
accomplishment, and other such statues reports should be accurate and current at all times.
Documents that are considered confidential or that contain sensitive data will not be sent
electronically. If such documents are required, the employee may incur fees for the documents
being sent.

Changes must be communicated/updated within 30 days of the information change taking
effect. Former Employees do not have access to their files other than documents that must be
provided per written request based on state and federal law.

Liquidating 401K
If you leave your employer before retirement age, in most cases you will be able to transfer your
account balance out of your employer’s plan. If an Employee was employed for less than the
time required for the 401K to fully vest or had only recently begun making contributions to their
401K account prior to their termination, additional liquidation options may exist.

Warning:
o You may owe current income taxes – and possibly tax penalties – on your distribution if you
take money out before your legal retirement age unless you transfer it to an IRA or another
tax-qualified retirement plan.
o Taking all or a portion of your funds out of your account before retirement age will mean
you have less in retirement benefits.
Please see the plan administrator and your personal financial and legal advisor(s) for assistance
with handling your account.

Accessing W-2’s
To access your W-2’s at any time after they have been produced each year, utilize the following
steps:
o Log into www.Paycor.com with your username and password.
o If you forgot your login credentials, you can always click the “Forgot Username” or “Forgot
Password” for assistance in remembering or resetting your credentials.
o Print your W-2’s directly from the Paycor system.
o If you Change your address you need to notify your payroll department.

Timekeeping & Payroll

Time Records
Please see your direct Supervisor for details regarding what methods you should be using to
record and report your work times as these vary based on your brand and position.
Employees are required to clock in when they report to work and clock out when they leave.
Employees must clock in no earlier than five (5) minutes prior to the start of their scheduled
shift and clock out no later than fifteen (15) minutes after the end of their scheduled shift unless
approved by Management. Employees who are the scheduled openers for their location must
arrive for their shift in time to ensure all opening duties are performed properly prior to the
locations opening time. This ensures that the brand standards are able to be upheld for all
customers.
Direct Supervisors must verify the daily and weekly hours worked by all their Employees and
report and those to Payroll as required. Please meet with your direct Supervisor for additional
details regarding these deadlines. Hourly Employees must review their daily and weekly hours

worked as reported to Payroll by their direct Supervisor and sign off to confirm their accuracy.
Any discrepancies should be reported to your direct Supervisor immediately. Please see your
Supervisor for details regarding how this verification process is handled for your brand and
position.

Schedule Requests/General availability Changes
Management will make its best effort to accommodate schedule requests turned in with enough
advanced notice on a first come first served basis, provided the request can be accomplished
without adversely affecting business operations or teaming.
General availability changes should be submitted at least two (2) weeks in advance or as soon as
the employee is aware that changes are needed. Management will make its best effort to
accommodate general availability changes provided the change can be accomplished without
adversely affecting business operations or teaming needs. Schedule requests and general
availability changes after the work schedule has been determined will not be honored.
Employees must submit all schedule requests and changes to general availability in the
employee Personnel Platform System.
o Sun Tan City – MyGlow
o Buff City Soap – MyGlow
o Crunch Fitness – Woven
Schedule requests and general availability changes that fundamentally alter when employees
are available to work may result in dismissal from their position if the changes cannot be
accommodated due to business needs.

Shift Replacement
Shift trading between employees disrupts company operations and is generally discouraged.
However, in emergency situations, employees may trade shifts with prior approval from
management. It is the responsibility of the employee to find a replacement for their shift. If an
employee is unable to work due to illness, emergency, or unforeseen circumstances, they must
immediately call and speak directly with their supervisor to notify them of the situation.
Employees should provide at least two hours’ notice when calling in as a courtesy to colleagues.
In the event of an emergency where two hours’ notice is not possible the employee must
contact their supervisor directly by phone immediately. Texting is NOT an acceptable method of
communication a phone call is required.

Seminar/Webinar Attendance
If you are enrolled in a seminar/webinar and do not attend the seminar without notifying your
Supervisor, it is considered a no call no show to a scheduled shift. If you cannot attend a
seminar/webinar you are scheduled for, you must notify your Supervisor via a personal phone
call. Notice of a call-in should not occur “last minute” and should be completed at least two (2)
hours in advance out of courtesy to fellow Employees. In cases of emergency where two (2)
hours advance notice is not possible (accident, etc.), you must contact your Supervisor via direct
phone call immediately.

Meal and Rest Policy
During your employment with The Company, you will be expected to take meal and rest period
breaks in accordance with this policy. The Company recognizes that meal and rest periods are
an important part of the workday. By allowing nourishment and rest, they help foster Employee
wellness and contribute to productivity and safety in the workplace.
Due to the nature of the work environment at The Company, breaks are not scheduled.
Employees are allowed to take an informal break as deemed necessary, without clocking out, so
long as a team member is in the building. Anytime an Employee leaves the premises, they are
required to clock out, unless they are conducting company business.

Overtime
Employees may be scheduled to work overtime hours when necessary. When possible, advance
notification of these mandatory assignments will be provided. All overtime work must receive
the Supervisor’s prior authorization. Overtime assignments will be distributed as equitably as
practical to all qualified employees to perform the required work. Failure to work scheduled
overtime or overtime worked without prior authorization from the Supervisor may result in
disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
Overtime compensation is paid to all non-exempt Employees (1.5x regular hourly pay) after
forty (40) hours worked within a single week. This is in accordance with federal and state wage
and hour restrictions. Overtime pay is based on actual hours worked. Time off on vacation leave,
holidays, or any leave of absence will not be considered hours worked for purposes of
performing overtime calculations. Exempt Employees will not receive overtime pay unless
required by law.

Pay Periods
Employees are paid on a bi-weekly basis. Payroll is processed on Wednesday of the payroll week
for the previous pay period. Employees are paid all wages due per federal and state laws on a bi-
weekly basis. Employees are required to use the direct deposit payment option available. All
Employees can access paystubs electronically through Paycor. Please see your Supervisor for
assistance with gaining access to your Paycor record.

Bonus Policy
Bonuses are performance-based and contingent on meeting or exceeding pre-defined goals and
minimums. Bonuses are paid at the discretion of The Company and are not “commissions”. Any
Employee working at multiple locations will be paid bonus based on their performance average
from all locations.
Bonuses are paid on the last paycheck of the following month. Payment of bonuses requires
100% job attendance and successful completion of all assigned tasks. Any Employee dishonestly
handling transactions or promotions will be denied any bonuses that have not yet been paid and
will be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
If an employee decides to end employment, the employee must complete the required notice to
receive any bonuses that have not yet been paid out. All bonus plans are subject to change with

one day’s notice. Please see your Supervisor regarding brand’s bonus policies and incentive pay
programs to find those that apply to your specific position.

Payroll Deductions
The Company withholds all federal, state, and local taxes as required by law and IRS guidelines.
All bonuses, special pay, and prizes employees receive are taxable. Employee premium
payments for their elected insurance benefits are also collected via payroll deductions unless
the Employee is on leave during which other payment arrangements will be made. (See also
Employee Insurance Benefits section for more details).

Garnishment of Employee Wages
The Company will comply with all federal and state laws regarding the garnishment of Employee
wages.
Travel time/cost reimbursements (for travel NOT requiring overnight stays)
Travel time/mileage reimbursements vary depending on employee job type, position,
department, reason for travel, the distance of travel required, and whether or not the travel was
voluntary or required. All travel time/mileage reimbursements require approval from your direct
Supervisor.
PRIOR to each date of travel, Employees must meet with their direct Supervisor for details and
instructions regarding how their specific travel time/costs reimbursements will be handled. All
reimbursements are paid in accordance with all federal and state law requirements.

Overnight Travel Reimbursement
Travel time/expense reimbursements for work requiring overnight stays away from your home
community include:
o Reimbursements for meals during the time away from your home community. (Limited to
The Company approved per day max).
o Reimbursements for travel costs and related travel expenses such as parking/luggage fees,
as approved by your direct Supervisor.
PRIOR to each date of travel, Employees must meet with their direct Supervisor for details and
instructions regarding how their specific travel time/costs reimbursements will be handled. All
reimbursements are paid in accordance with all federal and state law requirements. Meal
allowances are set at $35 per day. Snacks purchased between meals, including hot and cold
drinks, as well as alcohol, are not reimbursable.
Documentation: All meal expenses must be accompanied by a cash register or credit card
itemized voucher with the detail. Restaurant guest check and tear-tabs are not acceptable.
Documentation of meals and entertainment expenses must include the following:
o Date and name of restaurant.
o Name of attendees and business relationship (including company name).
o Business purpose. All guests and Employee names must be listed on the expense report;
“Staff” is not acceptable. The cost of meals and entertainment attended by an Employee’s

spouse or companion(s) is considered personal and no portion of the expense is
reimbursable, including the Employee’s portion.

Error in Pay
All Employees should review their paystubs for accuracy each pay period. If an Employee notices
an error in their pay, they must notify their Supervisor immediately. The Company will make
every attempt to adjust no later than the next pay period.

chunks.locator: Page 40 — Fair Labor Standard Act (FSLA) – Safe Harbor Policy
chunks.section: Fair Labor Standard Act (FSLA) – Safe Harbor Policy
chunks.content:
Fair Labor Standard Act (FSLA) – Safe Harbor Policy
The Company intends to comply with all federal regulations with respect to the Fair Standards
Act (FSLA). In this regard, the FSLA provides an exemption from both minimum wage and
overtime payment for Employees employed in bona fide executive, administrative, professional,
computer, and outside sales positions. To qualify for an overtime exemption, an Employee
generally must be paid no less than $35,568 a year or $684 per week on a salary basis.
Being paid on a “salary basis” refers to an Employee who regularly receives a predetermined
amount of compensation each pay period on a weekly or less frequent basis which cannot be
reduced because of variations in the quality or quantity of work.
Subject to the exceptions listed below, an exempt (salaried) Employee must receive his or her
full salary for any workweek in which the Employee performs any work, regardless of the
number of days or hours worked.
o Exempt (salaried) Employees do not need to be paid for any work week in which they
perform no work and will not be paid unless appropriate accrued paid leave is utilized.
o If the Employee is ready, willing, and able to work, deductions may not be made for time
when work is not available.
Deductions from pay are permissible when an exempt (salaried) Employee is:
o Absent from work for one or more full days, or partial days for personal reasons, illness, or
disability.
o On an unpaid disciplinary suspension for one or more full days, imposed in good faith for
workplace conduct rule infractions or infractions of safety rules of major significance.
o In the initial or final week of employment.
o Taking unpaid leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act.

sections.heading: Fair Labor Standard Act (FSLA) – Safe Harbor Policy

chunks.content:
Important Notes:
o Exempt (salaried) Employees must use their accrued PTO, as instructed (See the Paid Time
Off (PTO) section), to receive pay for days where they are absent from work for personal
reasons, illness, or disability, and to ensure they have enough hours reported combining
their actual hours worked and their PTO hours to retain their full-time Employee status.
o PTO may not be utilized when an Employee is placed on unpaid suspension. (See the Paid
Time Off (PTO) section).
o Finally, as a public sector employer, The Company operates under principles of public
accountability, which permit deductions from the pay of an exempt (salaried) Employee for

partial-day or full-day absences due to illness, injury, or personal reasons when accrued paid
leave is not used by an Employee because:
o The Employee has not yet qualified to receive PTO.
o Permission for PTO use has not been sought or has been sought and denied.
o Accrued PTO has been exhausted (See the Paid Time Off (PTO) section).
o For all full-time Employees, time off without pay that would result in the total hours worked
by the Employee in any workweek dropping below thirty (30) hours is not permitted without
prior written approval from your Supervisor and the Human Resources department.
o The Company has classified those positions which are considered to be “exempt”.
o It is the policy of The Company to comply with the “salary basis” requirements of the FLSA
regarding exempt Employees.
o If you believe that an improper deduction has been made to your salary, you should
immediately report this information to Human Resources.
o Reports of an improper deduction from wages will be promptly investigated. If it is
determined that an improper deduction has occurred, you will be promptly reimbursed
(typically on the next regular pay date) for any improper deduction.

Salary Administration
The salary administration program at The Company was created to achieve consistent pay
practices, comply with federal and state laws, mirror our commitment to Equal Employment
Opportunity, and offer competitive salaries within our labor market.
Compensation for every position is determined by several factors which includes job analysis
and evaluation, essential job duties, and responsibilities of the job. Merit-based pay adjustments
may be awardee in conjunction with superior employee performance during the annual
performance evaluation process.

Employee Benefits

Paid time Off (PTO)
Paid Time Off (PTO) hours are hours issued to eligible employees that can be used for paid time
away from work for vacation, personal time, personal illness, or time off to care for dependents.
The PTO policy replaces sick, absence, personal, and vacation time. All state and local guidelines
regarding mandated additional sick time will be followed.

Eligibility
All salaried managers, full-time corporate office personnel, and full-time Assistant Salon
Directors/Assistant Makery Managers begin accruing PTO after 90 days of employment in that
position. PTO is not issued to temporary or contract employees.

Provisions
For qualifying full-time Employees, PTO accrues as follows:
o 90 days – 4 years of service in a full-time position – 2 weeks (80 hours), with a maximum
accrual cap of 120 hours.

o 5-9 years of service in a full-time position – 3 weeks (120 hours), with a maximum accrual
cap of 160 hours.
o 10+ years of service in a full-time position – 4 weeks (160 hours), with a maximum accrual
cap of 200 hours
Unused PTO is carried over from one calendar year to the next; however, employees may not
exceed the accrual cap for their respective tier. Once the cap is reached, no further PTO accrual
will occur until PTO is used and the balance drops below the cap.

Usage
Qualified salaried Employees must schedule PTO in half day (4 hours), or full day (8 hours)
increments only. No PTO is permitted during peak business seasons as listed below:
o Sun Tan City – February 1 and June 1
o Buff City Soap – November 1 and December 31
o Crunch – January 1 and February 28
PTO should be requested in the Personnel System at least two weeks in advance. In unforeseen
circumstances where advance notice is not possible, employees must notify their supervisor
directly via phone immediately and enter the PTO request into the Personnel System as soon as
possible.
PTO must be approved by the immediate Supervisor. PTO will be granted so long as it does not
place undue hardship on the business. Only one team member from a location/department will
be approved to take PTWO at the same time unless otherwise approved by the supervisor.
All State and Federal guidelines will be followed regarding paying out accrued PTO upon
termination of employment.

Holiday Benefits
Each FT salaried manager and FT corporate staff member will receive 8 hours of pay for each
holiday.

Corporate Office:
The Corporate Office is closed on the below listed holidays. These holidays are paid holidays for
salaried managers and full-time staff:
o New Years Day
o Thanksgiving Day
o Christmas Day
o Memorial Day
o Independence Day
o Labor Day

Sun Tan City:
Sun Tan City is closed on the below listed holidays. These holidays are paid holidays for salaried
managers and full-time staff:

o New Years Day
o Independence Day
o Thanksgiving Day
o Christmas Day
o Easter
The salons will be open on Memorial Day.

Crunch Fitness:
Crunch Fitness is closed on the below listed holidays. These holidays are paid holidays for
salaried managers and full-time staff:
o Thanksgiving Day
o Christmas Day

Buff City Soap:
Buff City Soap is closed on the below listed holidays. These holidays are paid holidays for
salaried managers and full-time staff:
o Independence Day
o Thanksgiving Day
o Christmas Day
o New Years Day
o Easter
Additionally, the locations that are open for business on Memorial Day, Independence Day and
Labor Day, hourly Employees will be paid 1.5 times their regular wage for hours worked on this
day. While FT salaried managers, DM and RDO will receive holiday pay. Holiday pay can be
banked into PTO in increments of 4 hours for individuals who work regular hours on holiday
weeks. Overtime pay is based on actual hours worked. Holiday hours will not be considered
hours worked for purposes of performing overtime calculations.

chunks.locator: Page 43 — Employee Discounts for Company Products and Services
chunks.section: Employee Discounts for Company Products and Services
chunks.content:
Employee Discounts for Company Products and Services
The Company offers discounts on products and services to Employees hired through Sun Tan

Group Health Plan Continuation Coverage Under COBRA
The Federal Consolidated Ominous Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA) requires continuation
coverage to be offered to covered employees, their spouses, their former spouses, and their
dependent children when group health coverage would otherwise be lost due to certain specific
events. Under COBRA, group health coverage is an arrangement that provides medical care.
This does not include life and disability benefits.
Those events include the death of a covered Employee, termination or reduction in the hours of
a covered Employee’s employment for reasons other than gross misconduct, divorce, or legal
separation from a covered Employee, and a child’s loss of dependent status (and therefore
coverage) under the plan. COBRA continuation coverage only lasts for a limited period of time.
The Company provides each covered Employee and spouse (if any) with written notice
explaining COBRA continuation coverage, when it may become available to you and your family,
and what you need to do to protect your right to get it.

Leave Requests

Family Medical Leave
The Company provides family leaves of absence without pay to eligible Employees who wish to
take time off from work duties to fulfill family obligations relating directly to childbirth,
adoption, or placement of a foster child; or to care for a child, spouse, or parent with a serious
health condition. A serious health condition means an illness, injury, impairment, or physical or
mental condition that involves inpatient care in a hospital, hospice, or residential medical care
facility, or continuing treatment by a health care provider. Eligible Employees may request
family leave only after having completed one year of service and worked at least 1250 hours. Eligible Employees should make requests for family leave to their Supervisors at least 30 days in
advance of foreseeable events and as soon as possible for unforeseeable events. Employees
requesting family leave related to the serious health condition of a child, spouse, or parent may
be required to submit a health care provider’s statement verifying the need for a family leave to
provide care, its beginning and expected ending dates, and the estimated time required. Eligible
Employees may request up to a maximum of 12 weeks of family leave within any 12-month
period. Any combination of family leave and medical leave may not exceed this maximum limit. If this initial period of absence proves insufficient, consideration will be given to a written
request for a single extension of no more than 30 calendar days.

Bereavement Leave
Employees who wish to take time off due to the death of an immediate family member should
notify their Supervisor and payroll immediately. Up to 3 consecutive days of paid Bereavement
Leave will be provided to all Employees provided the leave is approved and the days requested
are days the Employee was already scheduled to work. If the Employee was not scheduled to
work during the requested days, they would not receive pay as no bereavement time would be
required. The 3 consecutive days requested should include the day of the funeral and 2 days
either immediately prior to or immediately following the day of the funeral.
For the purposes of the Bereavement Policy, The Company defines “immediate family” as the
Employee’s spouse, parent, child, sibling; the Employee’s spouse’s parent, child, or sibling; the
Employee’s spouse’s grandparents or grandchildren. Special consideration will also be given to
any person whose association with the Employee was similar to any of the above relationships.
The Company reserves the right to request documentation, such as an obituary or funeral
program, or a prayer card from the Employee. These should be submitted at the time of
request or upon return from leave. As an alternative to this documentation, you may provide
the name of the deceased, date of death, city of death, and relationship to the deceased within
the request.

After receiving the approved request, the Human Resources Department will submit the
Bereavement days in your personnel profile under the PTO section. This will not deduct from
your PTO balance.

The Company will ensure that Employees who need time off for jury duty are granted the

The Company will provide paid leave when an Employee must serve on a jury. You will be paid

Employees can use available PTO to receive compensation for the period of this absence.

Maternity Leave
The Company does not offer paid maternity leave however; Employees are encouraged to use
any accrued PTO during this time. Additionally, under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA),
an Employee that has worked at least 1250 hours in the past 12 months is entitled to 12 weeks
of unpaid job-protected leave. While the time off cannot be taken into consideration for future
promotions, there is nothing that requires an Employee’s benefits, such as vacation time or
seniority, to accrue while they are on FMLA leave. Bonuses and other incentive pay (for sales,
etc.) do not have to be paid if they are not earned. The leave can be taken intermittently if the
Employee chooses to return to work on a part-time basis.
Health insurance will be maintained, but the Employee is responsible for maintaining their own
group health benefit premiums. If the employer opts to pay, they are allowed to recover the
fees when the Employee returns to work. The FMLA protection ends after the 12 weeks. The
time frame and conditions of the leave should be in writing. The Department of Labor website
is: http://www.dol.gov/esa/regs/statutes/whd/fmla.htm#content
If an employee wishes to take any leave, a Leave Request Form must be filled out and turned in
to the District Manager. The Leave Request Form provides documentation for any leave taken,

Client Tanning Policies and Regulations (STC & Crunch ONLY)

Protecting the Client from Overexposing
It is important to understand how the tanning equipment works and it is the employee’s
responsibility to prevent clients from overexposure. As a guide to understanding tanning
equipment and accurately recommend tan times, please refer to the Tan Time Chart located at
each workstation.
It is up to the employee to determine the time of clients’ tanning sessions and follow up with
clients’ tan times on each visit based on their skin type and tanning history.
If a client disagrees with the employee’s judgement and demands a longer visit, follow these
steps:
o Provide an explanation for the recommended tan time and educate the client in a friendly
manner.
o If the client is using upgrade points and/or paying for an additional service to tan on that
visit, offer a Courtesy Tan in exchange for taking your recommendation.
o If the client still insists on going against the recommended time, allow the client to tan for
the desired time and place a detailed comment on the client’s insisted tan time.
Clients may tan only one time per day in the UV bed, and one time per day in the VersaSpa ®.
Our system will notify you if the person has already tanned for the day at one of the Sun Tan
City or Crunch Fitness’s locations. Never let a client coerce the employee into allowing two visits

Consent Forms (New Client Release Forms)
Every client must complete and sign a Sun Tan City consent form (New Client Release Form)
found in our system. Every client must also fill out the skin typing chart provided at the front
counter. There are no exceptions. All new clients must present a photo ID (If the client is a
minor, the parent or guardian must show a photo ID).

Eye Protection
All clients using a tanning bed must use some form of FDA approved eye protection. Closing the
eyes, wearing sunglasses or placing a towel over the face is not FDA approved eye protection.
The Company does not provide eyewear free of charge for sanitary reasons. We do provide
eyewear for clients to purchase. If the client does not have their own eyewear, they will need to
purchase a pair. It is your responsibility to make sure they have eyewear before allowing them
to tan. Simply ask: “May I please see your eyewear?” If they refuse to show the employee, the
employee may not put them in a bed.

VersaSpa® Recommendations
The FDA recommends the use of protective eyewear, lip balm, and nose filters during sunless
visits. It is not required that clients use the FDA recommended protection during their sunless
sessions; however, we want to educate the client’s on the items they have available to use.

Tanning While Pregnant
It is recommended that pregnant women consult their doctor before using the VersaSpa® an/or
tanning in the UV equipment. It is not at the discretion of the employee to turn away or provide
personal opinions to pregnant women wanting to use The Company’s services.

Tanning with Skin Cancer
It is The Company’s policy not to tan someone who we know has (or has had) skin cancer
without a written statement from the client’s doctor giving approval or stating that the risks
have been fully explained by their doctor.

Minors
The Company complies with all State and Federal laws regarding minors and tanning. Those
clients who are under the age of 18 must have the signed permission of a parent to be able to
tan at Sun Tan City. The parent must sign the consent form in our presence and must remain in
the salon while the minor is tanning. Check State Regulations module for further instruction on
minor tanning restrictions. No one under the age of 14 will be allowed to UV tan at any Sun Tan
City location however, clients at any age may use the VersaSpa®.

Children Left Unattended
No children under the age of 12 will be allowed to be left unattended on the premises of The
Company at any time.

One Tanner per Room
There is only one client allowed per tanning room. Equipment should not be activated if there is
more than one person in the tanning room. Exceptions include:
o Minors who are using the VersaSpa® are allowed to have a parent or legal guardian assist
them in the equipment room only.
o Service Animals are allowed in the tanning room with a client.
